reading.title: The Community Garden
paragraphs: When a small piece of land became available near the library, residents suggested turning it into a community garden. The site had been empty for years, and many people wanted a place where neighbors could meet.

Volunteers began by clearing the land and preparing the soil. Some people brought tools, while others shared seeds and gardening advice. Together, they built raised beds and a simple path through the garden.

The garden soon became a shared outdoor classroom. Children learned how plants grew, and experienced gardeners showed newcomers how to care for seedlings. People who had rarely spoken before started working side by side.
By the end of the first summer, the garden produced tomatoes, beans, and herbs. The harvest was useful, but many volunteers valued the friendships they had formed even more.
